[head=2][color=#6ab7d6]Cloning, Cybernetics, and Continuity[/color][/head]
Modern cloning can rebuild a body and imprint a recorded neural pattern. It cannot prove that consciousness continued through death. A restored person remembers what the stored template remembered when it was recorded, not what happened afterward. Crescent's institutions recognize continuity because property, debt, title, employment, and military command cannot be reinvented after every restoration.
[head=3][color=#6ab7d6]Templates and class[/color][/head]
Anchor Vaults can preserve neural templates through severe recurrence conditions. The important inequality is freshness. A noble, senior manager, or valuable specialist may update a protected template frequently; an ordinary worker or spacer may wake from a record weeks or months old, missing relationships, debts, injuries, promotions, and promises.
The Mandate normally preserves certified title, debt, oath, and feudal obligation. Workers' Union law emphasizes social identity and allows formal reassignment when a restored person rejects the old identity. Corporate policies may define who controls a template, how often it is updated, and which obligations survive a new sleeve.
[head=3][color=#6ab7d6]Sleeve drift[/color][/head]
Repeated imprinting can cause memory overlap, compulsions, identity rejection, and other neurological problems. Clinicians call the broad condition [bold]sleeve drift[/bold]; severe cases remain known as [bold]Sleever Psychosis[/bold]. Treatment can manage symptoms but cannot restore lived experience that was never recorded.
[head=3][color=#6ab7d6]Cybernetics during a Turning[/color][/head]
Cybernetics are ordinary infrastructure: workers use reinforced limbs and machine interfaces, pilots use neural controls, and medics replace damaged organs or senses. Crescent engineers distinguish [bold]wetware[/bold], which interfaces with memory and perception, from [bold]hardware[/bold], which replaces or augments the body.
Biological tissue and installed machinery may not share the same stable baseline. A Turning can restore old scar tissue around a newer socket, leave wetware mapped to memories the patient no longer has, or revert firmware and components. Crescent-grade implants store synchronization records and support emergency isolation, reducing the risk without eliminating it.
See the [color=#6ab7d6]Cloning[/color] medical guide for the practical cloning workflow.
